text: {"text_type":"methods","experiments_detected":["siRNA knockdown of GENE-X in HeLa cells with qPCR validation at 48 h","CellTiter-Glo proliferation assay of GENE-X-depleted HeLa cells at 72 h"],"overall_assessment":"The central claim that GENE-X is required for HeLa growth rests on one siRNA sequence, with no non-targeting control, no rescue, and knockdown confirmed only by qPCR with n = 2. The proliferation result (45% reduction) has no stated replicate number, control, or statistical test. The experiment would need a second siRNA, a non-targeting control, protein-level validation, a rescue, and a proper statistical analysis before the conclusion could be supported.","findings":[{"rule_id":"R06","title":"RNAi: at least two independent siRNA/shRNA sequences","severity":"critical","issue":"Only one siRNA against GENE-X is described. No second, non-overlapping siRNA or pooled-siRNA deconvolution is mentioned.","why_reviewers_care":"A single siRNA can produce a convincing but off-target phenotype, and reviewers expect two independent sequences giving the same result.","suggestion":"Repeat the knockdown and proliferation assay with at least one additional, non-overlapping siRNA against GENE-X and report that both reproduce the phenotype.","evidence":"50 nM siRNA targeting GENE-X"},{"rule_id":"R07","title":"RNAi: non-targeting control delivered the same way","severity":"critical","issue":"No non-targeting (scrambled) siRNA control is mentioned. The text does not say what the 45% reduction is measured against.","why_reviewers_care":"Transfection and RNAi machinery alter cell growth and interferon responses. Only a non-targeting siRNA delivered with the same reagent, concentration and duration separates target-specific effects from these.","suggestion":"Add a non-targeting siRNA transfected with Lipofectamine RNAiMAX at 50 nM for the same 48 h, and run it in the qPCR and CellTiter-Glo assays alongside the GENE-X siRNA. State this control in the Methods and use it as the reference for the 70% and 45% values.","evidence":"50 nM siRNA targeting GENE-X using Lipofectamine RNAiMAX"},{"rule_id":"R01","title":"Negative and positive controls","severity":"critical","issue":"No negative control (non-targeting siRNA, mock transfection, or untransfected cells) is named for either readout. No positive control for the proliferation assay is mentioned.","why_reviewers_care":"Without a matched negative control the 45% reduction cannot be attributed to GENE-X loss rather than transfection stress. Without a positive control, a negative result in this assay could not be interpreted.","suggestion":"Include a non-targeting siRNA as the matched negative control. Add a positive control for the proliferation readout, such as a siRNA against a known essential gene or a cytotoxic or antiproliferative compound at a stated dose.","evidence":"GENE-X-depleted cells showed a 45% reduction in proliferation measured by CellTiter-Glo at 72 h"},{"rule_id":"R11","title":"Rescue experiment","severity":"critical","issue":"No rescue experiment is described, yet the text concludes that GENE-X is required for HeLa growth. This is a single-siRNA experiment without rescue.","why_reviewers_care":"Rescue with an siRNA-resistant cDNA is the strongest evidence that a phenotype comes from loss of the intended target. Its absence, combined with a single siRNA, is a common reason for rejection.","suggestion":"Express an siRNA-resistant GENE-X cDNA (silent mutations in the siRNA target site) in GENE-X-depleted cells, with an empty-vector control, and show that the proliferation defect is reversed. Report the rescue expression level relative to endogenous GENE-X.","evidence":"indicating that GENE-X is required for HeLa cell growth"},{"rule_id":"R02","title":"Biological replicates and sample size","severity":"critical","issue":"The knockdown validation uses n = 2. It is not stated whether these are independent biological replicates (separate transfections) or technical qPCR replicates. The n for the proliferation assay is not given at all.","why_reviewers_care":"n = 2 is below the three independent biological replicates needed for inferential statistics. Technical replicates inflate apparent significance.","suggestion":"State what n counts. Perform at least three independent biological experiments, each with a separate siRNA transfection, and report n for both qPCR and the proliferation assay.","evidence":"70% reduction in GENE-X mRNA, n = 2"},{"rule_id":"R03","title":"Statistical test matches the design","severity":"critical","issue":"The 45% reduction in proliferation is presented as a difference, but no statistical test is named and no p-value is given.","why_reviewers_care":"A claim of difference without a stated, design-appropriate test cannot be evaluated and the conclusion is unsupported.","suggestion":"Specify the test (for example, an unpaired t-test on normalised values, or one-way ANOVA with Dunnett's correction if there are several siRNAs plus the non-targeting control). Report exact p-values and the number of independent experiments.","evidence":"GENE-X-depleted cells showed a 45% reduction in proliferation"},{"rule_id":"R04","title":"Statistics reporting in legends and methods","severity":"major","issue":"The text does not say what error bars or variation represent (SD, SEM, 95% CI), the n for the proliferation assay, the test name, or exact p-values.","why_reviewers_care":"Journal reporting checklists require these items. Without them the result cannot be assessed.","suggestion":"Add to the figure legend or Methods: n and what it counts, the error measure (for example SD of three independent experiments), the statistical test, and exact p-values.","evidence":"GENE-X-depleted cells showed a 45% reduction in proliferation measured by CellTiter-Glo at 72 h"},{"rule_id":"R08","title":"Knockdown / knockout validation","severity":"critical","issue":"Knockdown is shown only at the mRNA level by qPCR. Protein loss is not demonstrated, and protein detection is not mentioned as impossible. Validation was at 48 h, while the phenotype was read at 72 h, and the validation is not stated to be in the same cells under the same conditions. The 70% reduction is quantified, which is good.","why_reviewers_care":"mRNA reduction does not guarantee protein loss. A phenotype without proof of target depletion at the protein level cannot be attributed to the target.","suggestion":"Show GENE-X protein loss by western blot (with a validated antibody and loading control) at the time of the proliferation assay, or at least in the same cells, using the non-targeting siRNA as reference. If no antibody is available, state this and justify the mRNA-only approach.","evidence":"knockdown was confirmed by qPCR (70% reduction in GENE-X mRNA, n = 2)"},{"rule_id":"R12","title":"Reagent identity, normalization and loading controls","severity":"minor","issue":"The siRNA catalogue number or sequence is not listed. The HeLa source, authentication (for example STR profiling), and mycoplasma testing are not stated. The qPCR reference gene(s) and the quantification method (for example ddCt) are not named.","why_reviewers_care":"These are reproducibility requirements on most journals' checklists, and unauthenticated cell lines are a major cause of irreproducible results.","suggestion":"Add the siRNA supplier and catalogue number (or sequence), the HeLa source and STR authentication date, the mycoplasma test result, the qPCR reference gene(s) with a stability justification, and the quantification method.","evidence":"HeLa cells were transfected with 50 nM siRNA targeting GENE-X using Lipofectamine RNAiMAX"}],"satisfied":[],"not_applicable":["R05","R09","R10"]}

{"text_type":"methods","experiments_detected":["Lentiviral shRNA stable knockdown of GENE-Y in MCF7 cells with puromycin selection","qPCR validation of knockdown efficiency","Transwell migration assay comparing shGENE-Y cells with untransduced MCF7 cells"],"overall_assessment":"The central claim, that GENE-Y knockdown slows MCF7 migration 3-fold, rests on a single shRNA sequence, has no non-targeting or empty-vector control, and is validated only at the mRNA level. The statistics are computed on three wells rather than independent biological replicates, which invalidates the reported p-value. The experiment needs a second independent shRNA, a matched non-targeting control, protein-level validation, a rescue, and biological replicates before the migration phenotype can be attributed to GENE-Y.","findings":[{"rule_id":"R02","title":"Biological replicates and sample size","severity":"critical","issue":"The statistic is computed on n = 3 wells, which are technical replicates of one transduction and one population. No count of independent biological replicates (separate transductions or independent selected pools) is given.","why_reviewers_care":"Technical replicates measure pipetting precision, not biological variability. A p-value computed on wells from one culture is inflated and will not survive review.","suggestion":"Repeat the transwell assay with at least three independent biological replicates, meaning separately transduced and selected knockdown pools or independent experiments on different days. Report n as the number of independent experiments and analyse the per-experiment means (or use a mixed model with experiment as a random effect).","evidence":"n = 3 wells, p < 0.01, t-test"},{"rule_id":"R06","title":"RNAi: at least two independent siRNA/shRNA sequences","severity":"critical","issue":"Only one shRNA (pLKO.1-shGENE-Y) is used, and no second non-overlapping shRNA against GENE-Y is mentioned. No rescue is reported either.","why_reviewers_care":"Off-target effects of a single shRNA can produce a convincing but false migration phenotype. Two independent sequences giving the same result is the minimum standard.","suggestion":"Add at least one additional shRNA targeting a different region of GENE-Y (ideally from a different vector or sequence set) and show that it reproduces both the knockdown and the migration phenotype.","evidence":"MCF7 cells were transduced with lentiviral pLKO.1-shGENE-Y"},{"rule_id":"R07","title":"RNAi: non-targeting control delivered the same way","severity":"critical","issue":"The control is untransduced MCF7 cells. No non-targeting (scramble) shRNA or empty pLKO.1 vector was transduced and puromycin-selected in parallel.","why_reviewers_care":"Lentiviral transduction, puromycin selection, and shRNA expression alter cell physiology. Only a non-targeting shRNA processed identically separates target-specific effects from these.","suggestion":"Transduce a matched non-targeting shRNA (or empty pLKO.1) in parallel, select with puromycin for the same 7 days, and compare migration of shGENE-Y against this control as the primary comparison. Keep untransduced cells as an additional reference.","evidence":"Untransduced MCF7 cells served as control."},{"rule_id":"R01","title":"Negative and positive controls","severity":"major","issue":"The only control is untransduced cells, which do not undergo the same lentiviral transduction and puromycin selection as the knockdown cells. No positive control for the migration assay is mentioned.","why_reviewers_care":"Without a control handled identically except for the variable under test, the effect cannot be separated from transduction or selection stress. A positive control shows the transwell assay can detect a migration change.","suggestion":"Use the matched non-targeting shRNA or empty-vector line (see R07) as the negative control. Add a positive control for migration, such as a known migration inhibitor or stimulator for MCF7 cells, to confirm assay sensitivity.","evidence":"Untransduced MCF7 cells served as control."},{"rule_id":"R08","title":"Knockdown / knockout validation","severity":"critical","issue":"Knockdown is shown only as 80% reduction at the mRNA level by qPCR. Protein loss is not shown, and the qPCR reference genes are not named. It is not stated whether validation was done in the same cells, at the same time point, as the migration assay.","why_reviewers_care":"mRNA reduction does not guarantee protein loss. A phenotype without proof of target loss at the protein level cannot be attributed to the target.","suggestion":"Add a western blot or immunoblot for GENE-Y protein using a validated antibody (with the loss of signal in knockdown cells as evidence of specificity), with a loading control. Name the qPCR reference genes and their stability, state the quantification method (e.g. ddCt), and confirm that validation was done on the cells used in the transwell assay.","evidence":"Knockdown efficiency was 80% by qPCR."},{"rule_id":"R11","title":"Rescue experiment","severity":"critical","issue":"Migration is the main phenotype, and no rescue is reported. No siRNA/shRNA-resistant GENE-Y cDNA re-expression is described, and no empty-vector rescue control is mentioned.","why_reviewers_care":"Rescue is the strongest evidence that the phenotype is caused by loss of the intended target. With a single shRNA and no rescue, this omission is especially serious.","suggestion":"Re-express GENE-Y cDNA carrying silent mutations in the shRNA target site in shGENE-Y cells, with an empty-vector rescue control. Show that migration returns toward control levels, and report the expression level of the rescue construct relative to endogenous protein.","evidence":"shGENE-Y cells migrated 3-fold slower in transwell assays"},{"rule_id":"R04","title":"Statistics reporting in legends and methods","severity":"major","issue":"The text does not state what the variability measure represents (SD, SEM, or CI) or whether the migration data are shown as individual points or means. The n unit (wells) is given, but the p-value is reported only as a threshold without the exact value.","why_reviewers_care":"Journal reporting checklists require the error-bar definition, the n and its unit, the test name, and exact p-values or defined thresholds. Without them the result cannot be evaluated.","suggestion":"State in the legend: 'Data show mean ± SD of n = 3 independent experiments (each the mean of technical wells); two-tailed unpaired t-test; exact p value = X.' Give the exact p-value and state whether the test was one- or two-tailed.","evidence":"n = 3 wells, p < 0.01, t-test"},{"rule_id":"R05","title":"Blinding and randomization","severity":"major","issue":"Transwell migration is usually quantified by counting cells or measuring stained area. The text does not say whether the scorer was blinded to group identity or whether the sample order was randomized.","why_reviewers_care":"Unblinded scoring of migration is a well-documented source of bias. Reviewers expect a statement on blinding and on how quantification was performed.","suggestion":"State that cell counting was performed by a person blinded to sample identity (for example, samples were coded by a colleague), or describe the automated pipeline and confirm it was applied identically to all groups. Describe how the fields of view were chosen.","evidence":"shGENE-Y cells migrated 3-fold slower in transwell assays (n = 3 wells, p < 0.01, t-test)."},{"rule_id":"R03","title":"Statistical test matches the design","severity":"minor","issue":"A t-test is named for a two-group comparison, which fits the design. Whether it was paired or unpaired, one- or two-tailed, and whether normality was checked with n = 3 are not stated.","why_reviewers_care":"With very small n, normality cannot be verified, and a non-parametric alternative or a justification is expected. Paired versus unpaired status and tailedness must be stated.","suggestion":"Specify the t-test type (unpaired, two-tailed), state whether normality was assessed, and once biological replicates are increased (see R02), consider a non-parametric test or justify the parametric choice.","evidence":"p < 0.01, t-test"},{"rule_id":"R12","title":"Reagent identity, normalization and loading controls","severity":"minor","issue":"The shRNA sequence or catalogue number is not given (shGENE-Y is a placeholder). The source, STR authentication, and mycoplasma status of MCF7 cells are not stated. qPCR primers and reference genes are not listed. The passage range is not given.","why_reviewers_care":"These are reproducibility requirements on most journal checklists. Unauthenticated cell lines and unlisted shRNA sequences are common causes of irreproducible results.","suggestion":"Provide the shRNA target sequence and TRC or catalogue number, the MCF7 source and STR profile date, a mycoplasma test statement, the qPCR primer sequences and reference genes, and the passage range used.","evidence":"lentiviral pLKO.1-shGENE-Y"}],"satisfied":[{"rule_id":"R03","note":"A named t-test is an appropriate type for a two-group comparison of migration, although the details listed under R03 still need to be specified."}],"not_applicable":["R09","R10"]}

{"text_type":"methods","experiments_detected":["C. elegans feeding RNAi of gene-z (Ahringer library, HT115 dsRNA)","Brood size assay at day 1 of adulthood"],"overall_assessment":"The text describes a single C. elegans feeding-RNAi clone scored for brood size, with an empty L4440 vector control. The main risks are that the phenotype rests on one unverified RNAi clone, with no knockdown validation, no rescue, and an identity assumed from plate position. The statistical claim of a 35% reduction has no test, n, or variability reported, so the result cannot be evaluated as written. The experiment needs a verified clone, knockdown confirmation, a second independent RNAi clone or rescue, and full statistical reporting before the conclusion can be supported.","findings":[{"rule_id":"R06","title":"RNAi: at least two independent siRNA/shRNA sequences","severity":"critical","issue":"Only one RNAi clone against gene-z is used. No second, non-overlapping dsRNA clone (or second independent reagent) is described.","why_reviewers_care":"Off-target effects of a single dsRNA can produce a convincing but false brood-size phenotype. Two independent clones giving the same result is the minimum standard.","suggestion":"Add a second independent Ahringer (or ORFeome/other library) clone targeting a non-overlapping region of gene-z and show that it reproduces the 35% brood-size reduction. If only one clone is available, add a rescue experiment (see R11).","evidence":"dsRNA against gene-z from the Ahringer library"},{"rule_id":"R08","title":"Knockdown / knockout validation","severity":"critical","issue":"No evidence is given that gene-z mRNA or protein is reduced in the RNAi-fed worms. Knockdown is inferred only from the phenotype.","why_reviewers_care":"A phenotype without proof of target loss cannot be attributed to the target. The knockdown must be shown in the same animals and conditions as the phenotypic assay.","suggestion":"Quantify gene-z mRNA by qPCR (with validated reference genes, stated quantification method such as ddCt) in L4 or day-1 adult worms fed gene-z RNAi versus L4440, and report the percentage reduction. If an antibody or tagged reporter is available, show protein loss too.","evidence":"gene-z(RNAi) animals showed a 35% reduction in brood size"},{"rule_id":"R11","title":"Rescue experiment","severity":"critical","issue":"No rescue experiment is described, and the phenotype rests on a single RNAi clone.","why_reviewers_care":"Rescue is the strongest evidence that the phenotype is caused by loss of the intended target. Brood size per worm is a count, which affects the choice of test.","suggestion":"State the test used (for example Mann-Whitney U for per-worm brood sizes, or a negative-binomial/Poisson GLM for counts). Without a stated n and what it counts, the reliability of the 35% figure is unknown.","suggestion":"State the total number of worms scored per condition and the number of independent biological replicates (e.g. three independent synchronizations on separate days). Report the per-replicate values so reviewers can see reproducibility.","evidence":"Synchronized L1 worms were fed HT115 bacteria expressing dsRNA against gene-z"},{"rule_id":"R04","title":"Statistics reporting in legends and methods","severity":"major","issue":"The reported reduction lacks error or variability information, n, test name, and p-value.","why_reviewers_care":"Journal reporting checklists require these items, and without them the result cannot be assessed.","suggestion":"Report mean brood size ± SD or SEM (or median with IQR) for control and gene-z(RNAi), the exact n, the test name, the exact p-value, and what the error bars represent.","evidence":"brood size was scored and gene-z(RNAi) animals showed a 35% reduction in brood size"},{"rule_id":"R05","title":"Blinding and randomization","severity":"major","issue":"Brood size is scored by counting progeny, but it is not stated whether the scorer was blinded to RNAi condition or whether worms were randomly assigned to plates.","why_reviewers_care":"Unblinded counting is a known source of bias, especially for a subjective endpoint such as scoring of progeny or viability.","suggestion":"Add a statement that plates were coded so that the person counting progeny did not know the RNAi condition, and that worms or plates were randomly assigned. The clone was not sequence-verified, and the C. elegans strain is not stated.","why_reviewers_care":"Library plate positions are frequently mis-annotated, so the RNAi reagent may not target gene-z. Strain background is a basic reproducibility requirement.","suggestion":"Sequence the insert of the RNAi clone (or verify by PCR and sequencing of the cloned fragment) and state the clone ID and the sequenced target region. State the strain used (e.g. N2 Bristol) and its source, and the growth temperature.","evidence":"The identity of the RNAi clone was assumed from its position in the library plate."},{"rule_id":"R01","title":"Negative and positive controls","severity":"minor","issue":"A negative control is present, but no positive control is described for the RNAi or brood-size assay.","why_reviewers_care":"A positive control shows that the RNAi pipeline and the brood-size assay can detect a known phenotype, so a negative result can be interpreted.","suggestion":"Include a gene whose RNAi is known to reduce brood size (e.g. a well-characterised fertility gene) run in parallel with gene-z and L4440, and report it alongside the gene-z result.","evidence":"Worms fed bacteria carrying the empty L4440 vector served as control."}],"satisfied":[{"rule_id":"R01","note":"A matched negative control is used: worms fed the empty L4440 vector, handled in the same way as the RNAi-fed worms."},{"rule_id":"R07","note":"The control is delivered by the same route (feeding HT115 bacteria) and the empty L4440 vector is the standard non-targeting control for feeding RNAi."}],"not_applicable":["R09","R10"]}

{"text_type":"methods","experiments_detected":["CRISPR/Cas9 knockout of GENE-A in HEK293T using a single sgRNA (px459) with puromycin selection and single-clone isolation","Apoptosis assay under serum starvation comparing KO-7 clone with parental HEK293T cells"],"overall_assessment":"The central claim rests on one sgRNA and one clone (KO-7) with no rescue, no off-target assessment, and genotyping by PCR only, so the phenotype cannot yet be attributed to loss of GENE-A. The apoptosis result (2-fold increase) is reported without n, error bars, a named statistical test, or a p-value, so it cannot be evaluated. The control design also has gaps: the parental line lacks Cas9 and there is no matched non-starved comparison. Fixing these requires at least a second independent guide or clone, a rescue, protein-level validation, and a properly reported, replicated apoptosis assay.","findings":[{"rule_id":"R09","title":"CRISPR: multiple guides or clones, and the right controls","severity":"critical","issue":"Only one sgRNA ('a single sgRNA targeting exon 2') was used and only one clone (KO-7) was carried forward for 'all subsequent experiments'. Clonal derivation is stated, but no second guide or second independent clone is reported.","why_reviewers_care":"A phenotype from one guide and one clone may reflect an off-target cut or clone-specific artefacts such as clonal drift, aneuploidy or selection bottlenecks.","suggestion":"Generate a second KO line with a sgRNA targeting a different exon or site, and/or compare at least two additional independent clones from each guide. Confirm the phenotype is concordant across them and state which clones were used for each experiment.","evidence":"one clone (KO-7) with a frameshift deletion detected by PCR genotyping was used for all subsequent experiments"},{"rule_id":"R09","title":"CRISPR: multiple guides or clones, and the right controls","severity":"major","issue":"The control is 'Parental HEK293T cells', which do not express Cas9 because px459 was not present in them. Cas9 is therefore present in the KO line but not in the control. A non-targeting or safe-harbour sgRNA in a Cas9-expressing line is not described.","why_reviewers_care":"Cas9 expression and DNA-damage signalling can change apoptosis and stress responses. A Cas9-free control cannot separate GENE-A loss from Cas9 effects.","suggestion":"Add a control line that carries Cas9 and a non-targeting or AAVS1-targeting sgRNA, processed through the same selection and clonal derivation, and compare KO-7 against it in the apoptosis assay.","evidence":"Parental HEK293T cells served as the wild-type control."},{"rule_id":"R10","title":"CRISPR: off-target assessment","severity":"critical","issue":"No off-target assessment is stated. The guide design tool, its specificity score, predicted off-target sites, and any high-fidelity Cas9 variant are not named, and there is no concordant second guide or rescue.","why_reviewers_care":"With a single guide and no other safeguard, an unassessed off-target cut could produce the observed apoptosis phenotype.","suggestion":"Name the design tool and report its specificity score for the sgRNA. Sequence the top predicted off-target sites in KO-7, or add a second guide with concordant phenotype, or add an sgRNA-resistant rescue.","evidence":"one clone (KO-7) with a frameshift deletion detected by PCR genotyping was used for all subsequent experiments"},{"rule_id":"R11","title":"Rescue experiment","severity":"critical","issue":"No rescue is described. The apoptosis phenotype is not shown to be reversed by re-expressing GENE-A from an sgRNA-resistant cDNA, and no empty-vector rescue control is mentioned.","why_reviewers_care":"Rescue is the strongest evidence that the phenotype is caused by loss of the intended target. A single guide with no rescue is a common reason for rejection.","suggestion":"Re-express GENE-A cDNA carrying silent PAM or protospacer mutations in KO-7 at near-endogenous levels, with an empty-vector control, and show that the increased apoptosis under serum starvation is reversed. Alternatively, justify the omission explicitly.","evidence":"KO-7 cells displayed a 2-fold increase in apoptosis under serum starvation."},{"rule_id":"R08","title":"Knockdown / knockout validation","severity":"critical","issue":"Editing is inferred from 'a frameshift deletion detected by PCR genotyping'. The allele is not sequenced in the text, and loss of GENE-A protein is not shown by western blot or immunofluorescence.","why_reviewers_care":"A detected indel does not guarantee a null allele (in-frame deletions, alternative start sites, exon skipping), and mRNA or genotype data do not prove protein loss.","suggestion":"Sanger- or amplicon-sequence the edited locus and report the exact indel on each allele. Show loss of GENE-A protein by western blot with a validated antibody, using the same clone, passage and culture conditions as the apoptosis assay, and quantify the reduction relative to a loading control.","evidence":"one clone (KO-7) with a frameshift deletion detected by PCR genotyping was used for all subsequent experiments"},{"rule_id":"R02","title":"Biological replicates and sample size","severity":"major","issue":"The n for the 2-fold apoptosis increase is not stated, and it is not clear whether replicates are independent experiments, separate cultures, or wells.","why_reviewers_care":"Without a stated n and definition of replicates, the reliability of the 2-fold difference cannot be judged, and technical wells would inflate apparent significance.","suggestion":"State the number of independent biological experiments (at least three, each with its own culture and serum-starvation treatment) and the number of wells or technical replicates per experiment, and report the mean with variability across the independent experiments.","evidence":"KO-7 cells displayed a 2-fold increase in apoptosis under serum starvation."},{"rule_id":"R03","title":"Statistical test matches the design","severity":"critical","issue":"A claim of a 2-fold difference in apoptosis is made, but no statistical test is named or described. The design (two genotypes, with or without starvation) implies a two-factor analysis, which is not mentioned.","why_reviewers_care":"A claimed difference without a matched test has no supporting p-value. Two-factor designs need a two-way ANOVA with the interaction reported, or an equivalent.","suggestion":"Name the test used. For genotype by starvation, use two-way ANOVA with the interaction term, followed by a multiple-comparison correction. If apoptosis is a proportion, use an appropriate method for proportions, such as a binomial GLM or Fisher's exact test, and report the test.","evidence":"KO-7 cells displayed a 2-fold increase in apoptosis under serum starvation."},{"rule_id":"R04","title":"Statistics reporting in legends and methods","severity":"major","issue":"The text gives a fold change without an error measure, n, test name, exact p-value or threshold, or any description of how multiple comparisons were handled.","why_reviewers_care":"Journal reporting checklists require these items, and without them the apoptosis result cannot be evaluated.","suggestion":"Add a sentence such as: 'Apoptosis (% Annexin V-positive cells, mean ± SD of n = 3 independent experiments) was compared between KO-7 and parental cells under fed and starved conditions by two-way ANOVA with Tukey post hoc test; exact p-values are shown in the figure.'","evidence":"KO-7 cells displayed a 2-fold increase in apoptosis under serum starvation."},{"rule_id":"R01","title":"Negative and positive controls","severity":"major","issue":"The parental line serves as the genotype control, but the serum-starvation comparison has no matched non-starved (fed) control reported for each genotype. No positive control for the apoptosis assay (for example staurosporine) is mentioned.","why_reviewers_care":"Without a fed-condition control for each genotype, the increase under starvation cannot be separated from baseline differences in apoptosis or handling. Without a positive control, a negative result in the assay cannot be interpreted.","suggestion":"Measure apoptosis in both genotypes under fed and starved conditions, handled identically. Include a positive apoptosis control, such as staurosporine or another validated inducer, in the same assay run.","evidence":"KO-7 cells displayed a 2-fold increase in apoptosis under serum starvation."},{"rule_id":"R12","title":"Reagent identity, normalization and loading controls","severity":"minor","issue":"The sgRNA sequence, the px459 source or catalogue number, the HEK293T source and authentication (for example STR profile), and mycoplasma testing are not stated. The apoptosis assay kit or method is not named.","why_reviewers_care":"These are reproducibility requirements on most journal checklists, and unauthenticated cell lines are a common source of irreproducible results.","suggestion":"Add the sgRNA sequence and its target site, the plasmid source (Addgene ID is sufficient), the HEK293T source and STR authentication date, the mycoplasma test result, and the name and catalogue number of the apoptosis assay kit or antibody.","evidence":"GENE-A knockout HEK293T cells were generated by transfecting px459 encoding a single sgRNA targeting exon 2."}],"satisfied":[{"rule_id":"R01","note":"A parental HEK293T wild-type control is included for the genotype comparison, although the starvation-matched control still needs to be reported."}],"not_applicable":["R05","R06","R07"]}

{"text_type":"methods","experiments_detected":["CRISPRi knockdown of GENE-B in A549 cells expressing dCas9-KRAB, validated by qPCR","Cisplatin sensitivity (IC50) comparison between GENE-B-repressed and parental A549 cells"],"overall_assessment":"The main risks are a single sgRNA with no non-targeting control in the same dCas9-KRAB line, no rescue, and a parental Cas9-free comparator that cannot separate the knockdown from the reporter or transduction effects. The IC50 difference is reported with no n, no dose-response or viability method, no error estimate and no statistical test, so the claimed increase in cisplatin sensitivity is unsupported as written. The CRISPRi knockdown itself is quantified at mRNA level, which is a reasonable start.
